name: Congenital Macroglossia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Macroglossia

criteria.description: Presence of tongue enlargement exceeding normal size for age and sex at birth
Functional impairment including feeding difficulties, speech delay, or airway obstruction
Exclusion of acquired causes of macroglossia such as trauma, infection, or neoplasm
Identification of associated syndromes (e.g., Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome) as supportive

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital tongue enlargement with functional impairment and exclusion of acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging and genetic testing when indicated.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; genetic testing may reveal mutations in associated syndromes
imaging: MRI or CT scan showing tongue hypertrophy and exclusion of masses
Sleep study (polysomnography) for airway obstruction assessment
genetic: Mutations or epigenetic alterations in genes related to Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome or other overgrowth syndromes
other: Clinical evaluation of tongue size and function

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of macroglossia with abdominal wall defects, neonatal hypoglycemia, and organomegaly
Localized cystic lesions on tongue with characteristic imaging and histology
Macroglossia with systemic hypothyroid features such as lethargy and delayed growth

redFlags: Severe airway obstruction causing respiratory distress
Failure to thrive due to feeding impairment
references: Smith RJH, et al. Congenital Macroglossia: Clinical Features and Management. Otolaryngol Clin North Am. 2020.
